name: Compactly — your license, mapped to your next 13 weeks
one_liner: A free browser tool where a travel nurse drops photos of her license, BLS card and vaccine records and instantly gets a shareable map of the 43 compact states she can work in today, plus a timeline showing which credential expires mid-contract.
problem: For US travel nurses and allied travelers who take a new 13-week assignment three or four times a year. Today they keep credentials in a phone camera roll, a Google Drive folder and an agency portal, and answer the same two questions by hand every time a recruiter texts: can I take this contract on my current license, and will anything expire before it ends? Answering means opening NCSBN's site in one tab, squinting at a photo of a BLS card in another, and counting weeks on a calendar. Compactly makes it one drop: photos in, a personal map and an expiry timeline out, computed entirely in the browser so no document ever leaves the phone.
target_customer: US travel nurses, travel allied health and per-diem clinicians — r/TravelNursing (where credential-tracking threads recur), travel-nurse Facebook groups, nurse TikTok, and recruiters who would share it because it makes their candidates submission-ready. Free, open source, no account.
why_now: Vision LLMs cheap enough to read a phone photo of a BLS card in a client-side bring-your-own-key call landed this year (Gemini 2.5 Flash at $0.30/$2.50 per million tokens, PDF pages billed as images), and the compact map just moved again — Connecticut implemented 1 Oct 2025, taking the NLC to 43 jurisdictions, with Massachusetts enacted but targeting May 2027. The combination of a freshly-changed map and cheap client-side OCR is what makes the one-drop version possible now.
comparables: NCSBN Nurse Licensure Guidance (ncsbn.org) — the authoritative free tool: enter your residence state and target states, get official guidance and the NLC map. Gap: it knows nothing about your documents or their expiry dates, and produces nothing you would screenshot. GoodStanding (goodstanding.health) — free for individual providers, scans credential PDFs/photos and syncs expirations to Apple/Google/Outlook calendars; HealthTasks License Tracker and CerTracker do similar extraction-plus-reminders; NurseCred offers a credential wallet. Gap: all four are trackers — they answer 'when does this expire', never 'where can I work and does anything expire mid-contract'. Kamana is the closest shipped product for a credential wallet, but it is a profile you share with agencies, not a one-screen personal answer, and it requires an account. Compactly differs from all of them by doing one join nobody does — documents × compact map × a 13-week contract window — in one screen, with no login, nothing uploaded, and a screenshot as the output.
risks: Latent pain: nurses may shrug because their recruiter answers this for free, so the tool gets one screenshot and no return visit. The 43-state data has to be hand-maintained and stale data in healthcare compliance is worse than no data — mitigated by last-checked dates, linking to every board, and loud 'planning aid, not legal advice' framing. And the output is only as good as a phone photo of a worn BLS card; a misread expiry date is exactly the error that would make a nurse distrust it.
build_plan: Stack: single-page app, vanilla JS or Svelte, no backend, deployed on GitHub Pages; data stays in the browser (IndexedDB), model calls are bring-your-own Gemini API key stored locally. Steps: (1) Hand-compile the data file — 43 NLC jurisdictions plus Connecticut's Oct 2025 implementation and Massachusetts' pending status from the NCSBN list, each row carrying source URL and last-checked date, joined to a public state GeoJSON. (2) Drop zone that accepts photos/PDFs and calls Gemini 2.5 Flash with structured output: credential type, issuing state, licence number (never displayed in full), issue and expiry dates, multistate yes/no. (3) Render the map — green for states covered today, amber for compact-enacted-not-implemented, grey for states needing endorsement, with a per-state panel linking to that board's endorsement page. (4) Render the timeline — a 13-week bar from a date the user picks, with each credential's expiry plotted on it and a red flag on anything expiring inside the window. (5) 'Copy my card' button producing a clean PNG summary (states covered, soonest expiry, weeks of runway) with no licence numbers, plus a .ics download for every expiry. (6) Ship the data file and extraction prompt in the repo so nurses can correct state data by PR. CUT: accounts, storage, sharing links, agency features, endorsement fee and processing-time tables (no reliable dataset exists — link to each board instead), non-nursing professions, mobile apps.
launch_post: Travel nurses: drop photos of your license and certs and get one screen back — the 43 compact states you can work in right now, and whether anything expires mid-contract. Free, open source, nothing leaves your phone, no login. Built because the answer shouldn't take 20 minutes and four tabs.
reasoning: Won the build track because it turns one messy input into one personal, screenshot-shaped output that nobody currently produces, uses a dependency I verified is real and cheap, and shares nothing — audience, workflow or theme — with the manufacturing venture. It beat the changelog generator (git-cliff, release-please and GitHub's built-in generator already own that, free) and the Stripe payout explainer (nobody posts their payout data). Scored down on freshness because the map data itself is old news and NCSBN's free guidance tool exists; the newness is the client-side document read and the join. Could grow into a venture only in the direction Kamana already occupies, which is why it stays a build.
candidates_considered:
VENTURE — Quotefirst, RFQ triage desk for 10-200 employee machine shops: KEPT. Expressed pain, single decision-maker, buyer-side evidence on 24-hour quote expectations, narrow first version possible in weeks. · Dental confirmation/recall AI agent for independent practices (from @dentalops_raj): DROPPED after research — Weave (acquired TrueLark for $35M), NexHealth ($125M Series C), Arini, Dentina, Resonate and others already sell this to the same 1-3 location practice with PMS integrations; no defensible gap at a price a newcomer could charge. · Travel-nurse credentialing / portable credential file (from @nomad_nina): DROPPED as a venture — Kamana already offers a free clinician wallet plus paid agency portal and was acquired by Triage; Reddit evidence shows agencies resist third-party credential access for privacy and workflow reasons, so the blocker is policy, not software. · Multi-processor payout reconciliation for marketplaces/agencies (from @ledgerloop_ana): DROPPED pre-research as effectively the bookmarked company's own stated inbound, and Synder/Bookkeep already cover it. · Quarterly release-notes platform (from @tired_pm_lee): DROPPED as a venture — crowded (Released at $1.10-1.70/user/mo, LaunchNotes, Beamer, AnnounceKit) and Atlassian Rovo now drafts release notes natively inside Jira.

BUILD — Compactly, drop your credential photos and see where and how long you can work: KEPT. One input, one personal map-shaped output, no good free equivalent found, ships in a weekend with browser-only BYOK Gemini. · ChangelogSmith, paste Jira/Slack mess → customer-facing changelog: DROPPED — git-cliff, release-please, GitHub's built-in release notes and Rovo already do this free and are well known to the exact audience. · Payout Explainer, drop a Stripe payout CSV and see gross/fees/refunds/disputes reconstructed: DROPPED — low shareability, finance users will not paste real payout data into an unknown page, and Stripe's own payout reconciliation report covers it. · Machine shop map from Census CBP 332710: DROPPED — EveryJobShop and Kerfgrid already publish free browsable shop directories, and it shares the venture's audience, which the two-different-problems rule forbids.
research_notes: 18 tool calls: 3 reading-equivalent context queries, ~9 venture, ~6 build (no images in tonight's bookmarks, so the reading pot went to link-free context). What changed because of research: (1) The dental idea started as my front-runner and died on a single Perplexity pass — Weave's $35M TrueLark acquisition and NexHealth's $125M Series C, plus a follow-up showing Arini/Dentina/Resonate all selling Open Dental-integrated AI recall, meant the same buyer is already served at a fair price. (2) Travel-nurse credentialing looked wide open until a Reddit-sourced summary surfaced Kamana (free nurse wallet + paid agency portal, acquired by Triage) and nurse comments that agencies refuse third-party document access — so I moved that bookmark from the venture track to the build track and narrowed it to the nurse's own planning decision. (3) The manufacturing idea was reshaped twice: finding Uptool ($6M seed Feb 2026, published $195-495/mo, same emailed-RFQ-to-estimate workflow) closed the obvious pricing wedge, so I moved the product to the decision *before* the estimate — capability-fit triage against the shop's own machine list — after a targeted search confirmed Toolraw and Zetisis do capability scoring only on the buyer/marketplace side, not as a shop-owned intake desk. (4) I checked and discarded two statistics I would otherwise have quoted: the "78% buy from the first responder" and "30% never respond" figures both trace back to cross-industry lead-response studies, not manufacturing; the defensible number is the 2020 survey of 417 part buyers (67% expect a quote within 24 hours). (5) API costs verified for both prototypes: Gemini 2.5 Flash $0.30/$2.50 per million tokens with PDF pages billed as images, GPT-5 mini $0.25/$2.00. (6) For the build, I confirmed NCSBN's free Nurse Licensure Guidance tool and the 43-state NLC list exist (so the map alone is not novel), that no free downloadable NLC+fees dataset exists (so the data must be hand-compiled with last-checked dates), and that GoodStanding/HealthTasks/CerTracker/NurseCred track expirations but do not answer the "where can I work next" question — which is the join Compactly makes.
prototype_summary: Compactly is a two-screen prototype that turns simulated license-photo uploads into a map of the 43 compact states a Texas RN can work in today plus a 13-week contract timeline that flags a BLS card expiring in week 6.
